title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I may inform thee that I received a few lines from thee dated the 28 of the 12 mo, which was very agreeable to hear that thee has thy health so well. But are sorry to hear thy father & mother is so poorly, & that thy girl is gone, for I am afraid I cannot get Elizabeth Mull for thee but I shall endeavor to do the best I can. But underhanded dealing I don’t hold with. Itspossible there may be a way for it by spring, but cannot see any way at this time, so must leave it. & I may inform thee that I have been very poorly but am now a considerable better. The rest of the family in usual health, which I think a great favor. Sister Rebekah Warrington informed me that thee gave James a letter for her & that he believed he dropped it, for he did not know what became of it, & she desired me to write & let thee know of it in hopes that thee could give some account of it. I may inform thee of the decease of Silence Crispin which ate his supper in usual health & as I was informed was taken soon after with a fit of the colic, & was a corpse in half an hour after he was taken. Has left a poor afflicted widow that cannot take one step without help, nor has not this many years. As I have been informed he was buried this day three weeks. It will be agreeable to hear from thee often.

closer.salute: So I conclude & remain thy loving & affectionate mother,

postscript.p: PS Don’t expect to come soon, but should be glad to see thee if the way opens
